name: Spectral Theory

papers.title: Dirichlet eigenvalues of Laplacian with potential on general graphs and Weyl limits in integer lattice spaces $Z^d$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we first establish the existence of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian with a vertex weight on an infinite, connected and locally finite graph, via building compact embeddings of suitable spaces, when the weight decays faster at infinity than the optimal Hardy weight. In the particular integer lattice space $Z^d$, we apply a segmentation technique to estimate the mean Riesz potential over the entire space, thereby deriving estimates for the eigenvalue counting function and establishing the Weyl limit of the eigenvalues.

papers.title: Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO
papers.abstract: We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $\alpha\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,\alpha,\theta}$ is bounded from below by $d$.

papers.title: Localizing spectra and pseudospectra of a class of unbounded operators on Hilbert space
papers.abstract: We use a localization technique to bound and approximate the spectrum and the pseudospectra of a certain class of possibly non-normal, generally unbounded but closed operators on $L^2(X)$, where $X$ is either a) a locally compact second-countable Hausdorff group $G$, not necessarily Abelian, with identity, a proper metric, and a left Haar measure or it is b) a uniformly discrete subset of $G$ with the counting measure. We treat the discrete and continuous cases b) and a) simultaneously. Our results yield computable subsets and supersets of the pseudospectra of $H$ that converge to the corresponding pseudospectrum in Attouch-Wets distance as the size parameter $L$ in our localization procedure goes to infinity. We illustrate our findings with unbounded band operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb Z)$ and with Schr\"odinger operators with $L^\infty_{\rm loc}$ potentials acting on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$.

papers.title: The regular polygon maximizes the first positive Steklov eigenvalue among simple polygons at fixed area
papers.abstract: For $N\ge5$ and every simple planar polygon $P$ with at most $N$ sides, $\sqrt{|P|}\,\sigma_1(P)\le\sqrt{|R_N|}\,\sigma_1(R_N)$, where $\sigma_1$ is the first positive Steklov eigenvalue and $R_N$ is a regular $N$-gon. Equality holds precisely for polygons similar to $R_N$. This answers Oudet's fixed-area open problem \cite{AIM} for all $N\ge5$.

papers.title: Existence of single-resonance parametric bound states in the continuum: System of Schrödinger equations
papers.abstract: A bound state in the continuum (BIC) is an eigenmode of a linear wave system with its eigen-frequency embedded in the radiation continuum of scattering states. At the frequency of a BIC, scattering problems with given incident waves from infinity lose uniqueness. Due to their close connection with strong resonance effects, BICs have found many useful applications in classical and quantum wave systems. Existence theories of BICs have been established for some cases involving the so-called symmetry-protected BICs, Friedrich-Wintgen BICs, and Fabry-Perot BICs. The single-resonance parametric BICs (srp-BICs) are another important class of BICs. Such a BIC emerges from a single resonant state through tuning a real parameter. Using a simple system of two one-dimensional Schr\"odinger equations, we demonstrate the formation of srp-BICs and establish a rigorous existence theory.

papers.title: Genus one mirror symmetry and surfaces with trivial first Chern class
papers.abstract: The main goal of this paper is to study the extension of genus-one BCOV type mirror symmetry for smooth projective varieties with vanishing $c_1(X)$. We show that the naive generalization of the expectation that one can encode genus one Gromov-Witten invariants in the BCOV invariant of the mirror family cannot hold in this setup. We show this by completing the study of these invariants for surfaces. Progress had been made recently by Oberdieck's proof of the Klemm-Mari\~no conjecture for Enriques surfaces, which can be combined with computations of equivariant analytic torsion by Yoshikawa. We also perform the analogous study for bielliptic surfaces. Both of these cases present a sign issue not present in the known trivial canonical bundle cases, which we show implies that the mirror symmetry predictions cannot hold for varieties with torsion canonical bundle, even up to sign.

papers.title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schrödinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
papers.abstract: We consider the Schr\"odinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

papers.title: A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
papers.abstract: We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(\Delta + 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |\xi|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 d\xi,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
